notes.text: A flaw was found in js-yaml, a JavaScript YAML parser. An attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted YAML document that causes the parser to perform excessive processing when handling merge keys with empty sources. This can lead to prolonged CPU consumption, effectively causing a denial of service (DoS) for applications that process untrusted YAML input.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: js-yaml: js-yaml: Denial of Service vulnerability in YAML parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in js-yaml, affecting applications that process untrusted YAML input. The flaw allows an attacker to craft a small YAML document that, when parsed, can lead to prolonged CPU consumption due to inefficient merge key processing, potentially exhausting system resources. This is particularly relevant where applications handle external YAML data and have merge processing enabled by default.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.

notes.text:
A flaw was found in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver for version < 1.17.10 and < 2.9.1. 
Improper handling of data query elements in the GridFS component can lead to a file identifier being misinterpreted as a query. An authenticated user can exploit this to delete all GridFS file chunks, making stored file content unreadable, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the MongoDB Go Driver. The GridFS component does not properly sanitize caller-supplied file identifiers before using them in database queries. A structured document passed as a file ID (for example, a BSON document containing query operators) is interpreted as a query condition rather than a literal match value. An authenticated attacker who can influence the file identifier passed to GridFS operations such as Delete, DownloadToStream, or OpenDownloadStream in an affected application can exploit this to delete all chunks in a GridFS bucket, resulting in permanent data loss and denial of service.
The practical impact depends on whether the product's code passes externally-controlled values as GridFS file identifiers.

If upgrading go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver to version 1.17.10 (v1) or 2.9.1 (v2) is not immediately possible, the following steps can reduce exposure:
- Validate file identifiers before passing them to GridFS operations. Ensure that file IDs supplied by users or external systems are scalar values (e.g., primitive.ObjectID or string) and reject any structured BSON documents or maps. This prevents query operator injection.
- Restrict who can supply GridFS file identifiers. Do not allow unauthenticated or low-privilege users to directly control the file ID parameter in GridFS API calls (Delete, OpenDownloadStream, DownloadToStream, etc.).

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve cached responses, including sensitive session credentials like Set-Cookie values, belonging to other users. This occurs because the component fails to properly validate security-zeroed cache entries when processing client `max-stale` directives. By requesting the same URL with a large `max-stale` value, an attacker can obtain another user's session credentials from shared-cache entries that were intended to be secure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: http-cache-semantics: http-cache-semantics: Information Disclosure via max-stale directive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can bypass shared-cache security controls over the network and expose sensitive session credentials belonging to other users. Red Hat products vendoring this library in client-only command-line tools or local development utilities are at reduced risk, as triggering the defect depends on an intermediary or shared cache mechanism processing client cache-control directives. Environments hosting multi-tenant web applications or reverse proxies that evaluate HTTP cache headers via this component face direct exposure to cross-session credential disclosure.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. The lookupProperty own-property check returns Function.prototype.constructor before the prototype-method deny list is applied. When an attacker can render a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault enabled and an accessible function in the template context, arbitrary JavaScript can execute with the application process privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via Own Property Check Bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires rendering a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault set to true (off by default) and an accessible function in the template context, allowing bypass of the constructor deny list via Function.prototype. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because those non-default runtime conditions raise attack complexity (AC:H); default Handlebars configurations that keep allowProtoMethodsByDefault disabled are not exploitable for this issue.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. Incomplete validation of pre-parsed AST objects passed to compile() or precompile() allows unchecked AST fields to be emitted into generated JavaScript. An attacker who can supply an object instead of a template string can inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion in compile (Program.blockParams)
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires an application to pass a non-string object (for example, a JSON-deserialized value) to Handlebars.compile() or Handlebars.precompile(). Applications that only pass template strings are not affected. When that unsafe calling pattern is present, injected JavaScript can run with the privileges of the Node.js process. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because successful exploitation depends on that non-default API usage condition (AC:H), not on typical string-template pipelines alone.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost compress library. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a specially crafted Zstandard (zstd) compressed stream to an application using the library, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). Due to an integer handling error in the decompression logic, the decoder retains stale internal state and performs an out-of-bounds read, triggering an unhandled panic that crashes the application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via crafted zstd compressed input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost compress library's Zstandard (zstd) decompression implementation. An integer handling flaw in the FSE normalized count parsing logic allows a remote attacker to supply a specially crafted two-block compressed stream. When processed by vulnerable decode routines, the parser retains stale decode-table state and executes an out-of-bounds read, triggering an unhandled runtime panic. Applications decompressing untrusted inputs will terminate abruptly, causing a denial of service, while container boundaries and non-root execution isolate the impact from the underlying host.

remediations.details:
Reject or filter untrusted Zstandard-compressed payloads at ingress proxies, or restrict decompression endpoints to authenticated, trusted clients. No direct configuration-level workaround exists within the library itself.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-03) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce bounds on parsed count values and decode-table indices in klauspost/compress zstd decompression routines to prevent integer wraparound and out-of-bounds indexing: upgrade to klauspost/compress 1.20.2+ (or the corresponding fixed Red Hat builds), which reject counts exceeding math.MaxInt16 in readNCount, restrict Huffman-weight FSE tableLog values to 6 in huff0.ReadTable, and adjust count validation in validateNorm, closing crafted two-block zstd compressed stream. Until patched, this is a concern on applications decompressing untrusted Zstandard (zstd) input using klauspost/compress DecodeAll or streaming decoder, so reject or filter untrusted Zstandard-compressed payloads at ingress proxies, or restrict decompression endpoints to authenticated, trusted clients. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying integer wraparound defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1311 Input Size and Quantity Bounds Enforcement (high)

notes.text:
An update for gvisor-tap-vsock is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
A replacement for libslirp and VPNKit, written in pure Go. It is based on the network stack of gVisor. Compared to libslirp, gvisor-tap-vsock brings a configurable DNS server and dynamic port forwarding.

Security Fix(es):

* encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal (CVE-2026-33818)

* net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service (CVE-2026-56853)

* crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages (CVE-2026-56862)

* net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers (CVE-2026-78667)

* crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references (CVE-2026-97031)

* net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing (CVE-2026-94440)

* crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates (CVE-2026-111943)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

cwe.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

vulnerabilities.title: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in the mime/multipart and net/textproto packages in Go. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted multipart form request that bypasses configured memory limits when the remaining boundary limit is small. This issue allows the application to read an arbitrarily long line into memory, leading to excessive resource consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate severity for Red Hat products because, while an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger excessive memory consumption leading to a denial of service, exploitation cannot lead to code execution or information disclosure. The issue specifically threatens Go-based services and daemons that accept and process incoming multipart HTTP form payloads. Applications built with Go that do not expose web interfaces or parse multipart request streams are unaffected by this flaw.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in crypto/tls. A remote attacker can trigger this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet containing multiple Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) outer extension references to a server. Processing these unauthorized references leads to excessive memory consumption, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) through server crashes or unresponsiveness.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory exhaustion and crash server processes without requiring privileges or user interaction. Go applications that terminate TLS connections and accept Encrypted Client Hello configurations are vulnerable to resource amplification during the initial handshake. While the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data confidentiality, the resulting denial of service can disrupt critical network services.
notes.title: Statement

vulnerabilities.title: crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text:
Red Hat multicluster engine for Kubernetes v2.9 general availability release images, which provide security fixes, bug fixes, and updated container images.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.
A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE links in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
The multicluster engine for Kubernetes provides the foundational components
that are necessary for the centralized management of multiple
Kubernetes-based clusters across data centers, public clouds, and private
clouds.

You can use the engine to create new Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
clusters or to bring existing Kubernetes-based clusters under management by
importing them. After the clusters are managed, you can use the APIs that
are provided by the engine to distribute configuration based on placement
policy.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/html. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted HTML. When this arbitrary HTML is parsed and rendered, it can result in an unexpected HTML tree, bypassing input sanitization. This can be leveraged to execute Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution in applications that use the affected component.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/html: golang.org/x/net/html: Arbitrary code execution via Cross-Site Scripting
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important vulnerability in `golang.org/x/net/html` could enable remote attackers to execute Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution. The flaw allows specially crafted HTML to bypass input sanitization during parsing and rendering. Red Hat products are affected if they process untrusted HTML content using the vulnerable component without additional output encoding or robust content security policies.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/html. When arbitrary HTML is parsed and then rendered, it can result in an unexpected HTML tree. This allows an attacker to bypass HTML sanitization mechanisms, leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks in applications. Such attacks can result in information disclosure or arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/html: golang: golang.org/x/net/html: Cross-Site Scripting via HTML parsing bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability in `golang.org/x/net/html` is rated as Important. It allows for Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks by enabling an attacker to bypass HTML sanitization mechanisms when arbitrary HTML is parsed and rendered. This can lead to information disclosure or arbitrary code execution in affected applications. Exploitation typically requires user interaction, where a user processes specially crafted malicious HTML content.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `os.Root` functionality of Go on Unix systems. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass intended directory restrictions by crafting a path that ends with a symbolic link and a trailing slash. When a file is opened in `os.Root` with such a path, the symbolic link is improperly followed, potentially leading to access to locations outside of the defined root directory. This could result in information disclosure or unauthorized file system access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in Go's os.Root implementation. On Unix systems, `os.Root.Open()` improperly follows symlinks to locations outside the root directory when the path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., root.Open("symlink/")). This is because `openat()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` does not prevent symlink resolution when the path has a trailing /. An attacker able to create symlinks within an os.Root directory could use this to read or write files outside the intended root. The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected. This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

The following symbols are affected:
* `OpenInRoot`: Opens a file or directory within an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Create`: Creates a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Open`: Opens a path relative to an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenFile`: Opens a file with specified flags and permissions inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenRoot`: Opens a sub-root directory from an `os.Root`.
* `Root.ReadFile`: Reads a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.WriteFile`: Writes a file inside an `os.Root`.

There is no mitigation for this issue other than updating the Go toolchain to Go 1.25.12 or Go 1.26.5. Programs compiled with Go >= 1.24 that do not use the os.Root API are not affected by this vulnerability.
The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected.
This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenTelemetry-Go. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or invalid baggage headers. The `Parse` function, in affected versions, failed to reject raw-length inputs, leading to excessive processing and error logging when handling these large inputs.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation: OpenTelemetry-Go: Denial of Service via oversized baggage headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in OpenTelemetry-Go, affecting versions 1.41.0 and 1.43.0. An attacker can exploit this flaw by sending oversized baggage headers, causing the `Parse` function to process invalid inputs and log errors, which can lead to resource exhaustion and service disruption in Red Hat products utilizing these affected OpenTelemetry-Go versions. The impact is considered Important due to the potential for remote, unauthenticated denial of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/xml` package of Go. The `DecodeElement` function failed to correctly track recursion depth, which could lead to stack exhaustion. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML input, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important denial of service flaw affects applications utilizing the Go `encoding/xml` package. This vulnerability arises from an issue in XML decoding where a recursion depth counter fails to reset, potentially leading to stack exhaustion when processing malicious XML input.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/mod/sumdb. A malicious Go checksum database (GOSUMDB) can serve arbitrary module content that is not recorded in the transparency log. This allows a coordinated Go proxy (GOPROXY) and GOSUMDB to deliver malicious module content to a client, which cannot be detected by examining the transparency log. This vulnerability could lead to a supply chain compromise, allowing attackers to distribute malicious code.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/mod/sumdb: golang.org/x/mod/sumdb: Integrity bypass via malicious GOSUMDB
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important vulnerability in `golang.org/x/mod/sumdb` allows for a supply chain compromise where a malicious GOSUMDB can serve arbitrary module content, bypassing transparency log verification. This impacts the integrity of Go module dependencies in Red Hat products that utilize the Go toolchain and interact with GOSUMDB, posing a significant risk to development and deployment environments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/tlog. A malicious Go proxy (GOPROXY) could exploit this vulnerability by forging sumdb tiles. This allowed the proxy to bypass integrity checks and serve malicious module content to a local Go module cache, which would then go undetected by the transparency log. This could lead to a supply chain compromise where users unknowingly incorporate compromised modules.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/tlog: golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/tlog: Supply chain compromise via transparency log tile verification bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Exploitation of this vulnerability requires the victim to use a malicious or compromised Go module proxy (GOPROXY). The default GOPROXY (proxy.golang.org) is operated by Google. Users of custom or third-party Go proxies are at higher risk.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost/compress package. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted compression dictionary with an excessively large repeat value, triggering an integer overflow. When the dictionary is subsequently processed, this overflow leads to out-of-bounds memory access, crashing the application and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via integer overflow in dictionary processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as having an impact of Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker could trigger a denial of service by causing a process crash without requiring elevated permissions. In Red Hat environments where this Go library is embedded, exploitation requires that an application accepts untrusted dictionary structures for S2 compression and subsequently attempts encoding. Although the resulting memory access fault terminates the vulnerable process, the flaw is confined to process crashes and does not compromise data confidentiality or integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust process memory by sending millions of fragmented HTTP/2 DATA frames. Each fragmented frame is stored as a separate message, consuming disproportionate heap memory. This can lead to a runtime panic or out-of-memory termination, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via HTTP/2 DATA Frame Fragmentation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust memory and crash affected applications without exceeding connection flow-control windows. Within Red Hat OpenShift and containerized platforms, gRPC-Go is embedded in various internal control plane agents, monitoring exporters, and management components. Although services handling untrusted remote gRPC traffic remain susceptible to denial of service, exposure in standard cluster deployments is constrained because these interfaces typically operate across isolated internal networks or behind mutual TLS boundaries.

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve cached responses, including sensitive session credentials like Set-Cookie values, belonging to other users. This occurs because the component fails to properly validate security-zeroed cache entries when processing client `max-stale` directives. By requesting the same URL with a large `max-stale` value, an attacker can obtain another user's session credentials from shared-cache entries that were intended to be secure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: http-cache-semantics: http-cache-semantics: Information Disclosure via max-stale directive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can bypass shared-cache security controls over the network and expose sensitive session credentials belonging to other users. Red Hat products vendoring this library in client-only command-line tools or local development utilities are at reduced risk, as triggering the defect depends on an intermediary or shared cache mechanism processing client cache-control directives. Environments hosting multi-tenant web applications or reverse proxies that evaluate HTTP cache headers via this component face direct exposure to cross-session credential disclosure.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. The lookupProperty own-property check returns Function.prototype.constructor before the prototype-method deny list is applied. When an attacker can render a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault enabled and an accessible function in the template context, arbitrary JavaScript can execute with the application process privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via Own Property Check Bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires rendering a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault set to true (off by default) and an accessible function in the template context, allowing bypass of the constructor deny list via Function.prototype. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because those non-default runtime conditions raise attack complexity (AC:H); default Handlebars configurations that keep allowProtoMethodsByDefault disabled are not exploitable for this issue.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. Incomplete validation of pre-parsed AST objects passed to compile() or precompile() allows unchecked AST fields to be emitted into generated JavaScript. An attacker who can supply an object instead of a template string can inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion in compile (Program.blockParams)
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires an application to pass a non-string object (for example, a JSON-deserialized value) to Handlebars.compile() or Handlebars.precompile(). Applications that only pass template strings are not affected. When that unsafe calling pattern is present, injected JavaScript can run with the privileges of the Node.js process. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because successful exploitation depends on that non-default API usage condition (AC:H), not on typical string-template pipelines alone.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost compress library. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a specially crafted Zstandard (zstd) compressed stream to an application using the library, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). Due to an integer handling error in the decompression logic, the decoder retains stale internal state and performs an out-of-bounds read, triggering an unhandled panic that crashes the application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via crafted zstd compressed input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost compress library's Zstandard (zstd) decompression implementation. An integer handling flaw in the FSE normalized count parsing logic allows a remote attacker to supply a specially crafted two-block compressed stream. When processed by vulnerable decode routines, the parser retains stale decode-table state and executes an out-of-bounds read, triggering an unhandled runtime panic. Applications decompressing untrusted inputs will terminate abruptly, causing a denial of service, while container boundaries and non-root execution isolate the impact from the underlying host.

remediations.details:
Reject or filter untrusted Zstandard-compressed payloads at ingress proxies, or restrict decompression endpoints to authenticated, trusted clients. No direct configuration-level workaround exists within the library itself.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-03) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce bounds on parsed count values and decode-table indices in klauspost/compress zstd decompression routines to prevent integer wraparound and out-of-bounds indexing: upgrade to klauspost/compress 1.20.2+ (or the corresponding fixed Red Hat builds), which reject counts exceeding math.MaxInt16 in readNCount, restrict Huffman-weight FSE tableLog values to 6 in huff0.ReadTable, and adjust count validation in validateNorm, closing crafted two-block zstd compressed stream. Until patched, this is a concern on applications decompressing untrusted Zstandard (zstd) input using klauspost/compress DecodeAll or streaming decoder, so reject or filter untrusted Zstandard-compressed payloads at ingress proxies, or restrict decompression endpoints to authenticated, trusted clients. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying integer wraparound defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1311 Input Size and Quantity Bounds Enforcement (high)

notes.text:
Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes v2.16 general availability release images, which provide security fixes, bug fixes, and updated container images.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.
A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE links in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes provides the
capabilities to address common challenges that administrators and site
reliability engineers face as they work across a range of public and
private cloud environments. Clusters and applications are all visible and
managed from a single console—with security policy built in.

This advisory contains the container images for Red Hat Advanced Cluster
Management for Kubernetes, which add new features and enhancements, bug
fixes, and updated container images. See the following
Release Notes documentation, which will be updated shortly for this
release, for additional details about this release:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.16/html-single/release_notes/index#acm-release-notes

notes.text: On instances using Auth Proxy header authentication ([auth.proxy]) with identity caching enabled (sync_ttl > 0), two distinct user identities could produce the same cache key. An authenticated low-privileged user able to influence their own forwarded identity attributes could be served a higher-privileged user's cached session and act as that user for the duration of the cache TTL. Default configurations are not affected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: Grafana: Session takeover via Auth Proxy cache key collision
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact because successful exploitation allows an authenticated user to hijack sessions of administrative or privileged accounts, leading to complete compromise of the application. The flaw requires non-default settings where reverse proxy header-based authentication is enabled alongside active identity caching. In standard Red Hat product deployments, header-based proxy authentication is not enabled by default, which substantially limits the attack surface across standard installations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Grafana. When extracting plugin archives, Grafana did not safely resolve symbolic links. A remote attacker could craft a malicious plugin archive with symbolic links to escape the plugin installation directory. This allows the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute malicious code with the privileges of the Grafana server process, leading to remote code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: PLUGIN ARCHIVE EXTRACTION ESCAPES THE PLUGIN DIRECTORY, ALLOWING CODE EXECUTION
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Grafana's plugin extraction process is vulnerable to symbolic link traversal, enabling an attacker to write arbitrary files and achieve remote code execution with the privileges of the Grafana server. This critical flaw allows malicious code execution even before plugin signature verification, posing a significant risk in Red Hat deployments where Grafana is used.

remediations.details: While no configuration fully mitigates this issue, exposure can be reduced by limiting plugin installations to vetted and pinned sets of plugins from trusted sources. Additionally, disable the `plugin_admin_enabled` setting in the Grafana configuration if not required, to prevent non-administrator users from installing plugins. This can be done by setting `plugin_admin_enabled = false` in the `[plugins]` section of the `grafana.ini` configuration file. A restart of the Grafana service may be required for changes to take effect, which could temporarily impact service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in grpc-gateway up to v2.28.0. A remote attacker could exploit an incorrect access control vulnerability by sending a specially crafted POST request that includes the X-HTTP-Method-Override header. The application processes this header without restricting allowed methods, allowing the request method to be rewritten to an arbitrary attacker-supplied value before routing. This bypasses method-based access controls enforced by upstream proxies or Web Application Firewalls (WAFs), potentially leading to unauthorized actions or information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway: github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2: grpc-gateway: Access control bypass via X-HTTP-Method-Override header
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact for Red Hat products because exploitation requires a deployment where upstream reverse proxies or perimeter filters enforce access control solely based on HTTP methods without stripping method-override headers. In typical Red Hat deployments, backend gRPC services enforce their own authentication and authorization controls, limiting an attacker's ability to execute unauthorized actions simply by tunneling rewritten request verbs.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenTelemetry-Go. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or invalid baggage headers. The `Parse` function, in affected versions, failed to reject raw-length inputs, leading to excessive processing and error logging when handling these large inputs.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation: OpenTelemetry-Go: Denial of Service via oversized baggage headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in OpenTelemetry-Go, affecting versions 1.41.0 and 1.43.0. An attacker can exploit this flaw by sending oversized baggage headers, causing the `Parse` function to process invalid inputs and log errors, which can lead to resource exhaustion and service disruption in Red Hat products utilizing these affected OpenTelemetry-Go versions. The impact is considered Important due to the potential for remote, unauthenticated denial of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Grafana. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit the public dashboard query endpoint by sending arbitrarily large JSON payloads. This vulnerability, caused by a lack of request body size limits, triggers excessive memory allocation, leading to a denial of service through memory exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: Grafana: Denial of Service due to excessive memory allocation via large JSON payloads
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in Grafana, affecting Red Hat products that include Grafana. Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit the public dashboard query endpoint by sending large JSON payloads, leading to excessive memory allocation and potential service disruption. The absence of authentication requirements for exploitation increases the risk of widespread impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in go-git, a library used for Git operations. The component responsible for secure shell (SSH) communication does not correctly handle special characters in repository paths. This oversight allows a remote attacker to manipulate the command executed on the server by including a specially crafted repository path. This could result in the appending of additional shell commands, potentially leading to unintended actions on the system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/go-git/go-git: go-git: Shell command injection in SSH transport
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate: A shell command injection flaw in go-git's SSH transport allows an attacker to execute arbitrary commands by providing a specially crafted repository path. This affects Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes, where go-git is used for repository operations, potentially leading to compromise of the underlying system if an attacker can control the repository path. The impact is moderate due to the prerequisite of controlling the repository path.

notes.text: A flaw was found in oras-go. The file content store, intended to confine writes to a specified working directory, does not properly account for symbolic link (symlink) traversal. A remote attacker, by providing a specially crafted blob title, could exploit this vulnerability to create files outside the intended working directory. This filesystem boundary bypass allows for arbitrary file creation, potentially leading to unauthorized data modification or system compromise depending on the runtime environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in oras-go, a Go library used for managing OCI (Open Container Initiative) artifacts. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted tarball containing a malicious hardlink. When this tarball is extracted, the hardlink can be manipulated to point to files outside the intended extraction location, specifically within the victim's current working directory. This allows an attacker to read sensitive information from the system, and in some cases, could lead to unauthorized access to critical system files if the component is operating with elevated privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: oras-go: Oras-go: Information disclosure and arbitrary file access via crafted tarball hardlinks
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in oras-go. The ensureLinkPath tar extraction helper validates that a hardlink's target resolves inside the extract base directory, but returns the original unresolved target string instead of the validated path. When os.Link() is called with a relative Linkname, it resolves against the process's current working directory (CWD), not the extract directory. An attacker controlling an OCI registry can craft a tarball layer with a malicious hardlink entry whose relative Linkname escapes the extract directory, creating a hardlink to arbitrary files in the victim's CWD. Exploitation requires the victim to run `oras pull` (or code using the oras-go file store) against an attacker-controlled registry with auto-extract enabled (io.deis.oras.content.unpack annotation set to true). In typical Red Hat deployments, container registries are curated and trusted, reducing the likelihood of exploitation. The resulting hardlink shares an inode with the target file, allowing the attacker to read its contents through the extracted archive.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. The component failed to properly enforce source-address restrictions for several authentication methods, including password and keyboard-interactive callbacks. In applications that misuse the ServerConfig.PublicKeyCallback callback to make security relevant authorization decisions, an attacker with a valid key could bypass network-based access controls to gain additional privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Authentication bypass due to unenforced source-address restrictions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability severity is Important due to the requirement that an attacker already have a valid private key. A flaw in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh allows remote attackers to bypass source-address restrictions for certain authentication methods. This would allow an attacker to use a valid key for gaining additional privileges outside of the bounds of the network-based access controls.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/xml` package of Go. The `DecodeElement` function failed to correctly track recursion depth, which could lead to stack exhaustion. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML input, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important denial of service flaw affects applications utilizing the Go `encoding/xml` package. This vulnerability arises from an issue in XML decoding where a recursion depth counter fails to reset, potentially leading to stack exhaustion when processing malicious XML input.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost/compress package. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted compression dictionary with an excessively large repeat value, triggering an integer overflow. When the dictionary is subsequently processed, this overflow leads to out-of-bounds memory access, crashing the application and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via integer overflow in dictionary processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as having an impact of Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker could trigger a denial of service by causing a process crash without requiring elevated permissions. In Red Hat environments where this Go library is embedded, exploitation requires that an application accepts untrusted dictionary structures for S2 compression and subsequently attempts encoding. Although the resulting memory access fault terminates the vulnerable process, the flaw is confined to process crashes and does not compromise data confidentiality or integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in kin-openapi. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger a null-pointer dereference in the `openapi3filter.ValidateRequest` function. This occurs when validating a request against a `content` parameter whose `application/json` media type has no schema. Successful exploitation leads to a denial of service, causing request validation to panic and potentially resulting in an aborted request or a full process crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of Service via unauthenticated nil-pointer dereference
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Moderate severity because in Go services built on the standard net/http server — which includes all affected Red Hat products — panics inside HTTP handlers are recovered automatically per-goroutine. Only the individual request fails; the service continues to serve subsequent requests without data loss or state corruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in kin-openapi, a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. An unauthenticated client can exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted query with a large index in a deepObject query parameter. This forces the application to allocate multi-gigabyte memory, leading to an Out-of-Memory (OOM) error or a restart loop, effectively causing a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of Service via uncontrolled resource consumption in deepObject query parameter decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Important because a small request can exhaust memory and terminate an exposed service. Exploitation requires an application to decode attacker-controlled query parameters using kin-openapi’s deepObject handling with an array-containing schema. Schema limits such as maxItems do not prevent the allocation, and HTTP handler panic recovery does not protect against process termination from memory exhaustion.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go. The tlsConfigFromURI helper creates tls.Config values for amqps:// URIs without setting MinVersion. When the client is built with a Go toolchain whose default still permits TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1, a network attacker who can influence TLS negotiation may force an obsolete protocol version and weaken protection of AMQP messages and credentials. The issue is fixed in amqp091-go 1.13.0 by requiring TLS 1.2 as the minimum.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Missing Explicit TLS Minimum Version Configuration In URI Parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Red Hat product streams that ship amqp091-go before 1.13.0 are Affected because tlsConfigFromURI does not set an explicit TLS MinVersion when parsing AMQPS URIs. Exploitation requires a man-in-the-middle position on the path to the AMQP broker; Go 1.18 or later client defaults further raise complexity by preferring TLS 1.2 when MinVersion is unset. Streams that already ship amqp091-go 1.13.0 or later contain the explicit fix and are Not affected. The issue is not Critical because it is not remotely exploitable without those high-complexity prerequisites, and it does not provide unauthenticated remote code execution.

notes.text: RabbitMQ amqp091-go versions before 1.13.0 mishandle an oversized AMQP longstr field. A malicious or compromised broker can desynchronize message parsing, causing subsequent bytes to be interpreted as AMQP data and disrupting connection integrity or availability. Fixed in version 1.13.0.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Protocol Desynchronization and Frame Injection via Integer Overflow in readLongstr
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw affects Red Hat products using the vulnerable RabbitMQ amqp091-go client. Exploitation requires a malicious or compromised AMQP broker and may disrupt client connections or cause unintended protocol processing. Red Hat rates this issue Important.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri. This component improperly serializes the port component of a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) without validating its content. A remote attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious port value that injects authority delimiters. This manipulation can demote the intended host to user information and redirect the authority to an attacker-controlled host, leading to information disclosure as applications interpret the attacker's host as legitimate.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: Authority Injection via Unvalidated Port Serialization
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important flaw. Applications utilizing the `fast-uri` library in Red Hat environments are susceptible to authority injection if they process untrusted data as the port component of a URI. This could allow an attacker to redirect network traffic to an arbitrary host, compromising communication integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust process memory by sending millions of fragmented HTTP/2 DATA frames. Each fragmented frame is stored as a separate message, consuming disproportionate heap memory. This can lead to a runtime panic or out-of-memory termination, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via HTTP/2 DATA Frame Fragmentation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust memory and crash affected applications without exceeding connection flow-control windows. Within Red Hat OpenShift and containerized platforms, gRPC-Go is embedded in various internal control plane agents, monitoring exporters, and management components. Although services handling untrusted remote gRPC traffic remain susceptible to denial of service, exposure in standard cluster deployments is constrained because these interfaces typically operate across isolated internal networks or behind mutual TLS boundaries.

notes.text: A flaw was found in js-yaml, a JavaScript YAML parser. An attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted YAML document that causes the parser to perform excessive processing when handling merge keys with empty sources. This can lead to prolonged CPU consumption, effectively causing a denial of service (DoS) for applications that process untrusted YAML input.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: js-yaml: js-yaml: Denial of Service vulnerability in YAML parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in js-yaml, affecting applications that process untrusted YAML input. The flaw allows an attacker to craft a small YAML document that, when parsed, can lead to prolonged CPU consumption due to inefficient merge key processing, potentially exhausting system resources. This is particularly relevant where applications handle external YAML data and have merge processing enabled by default.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri. The library incorrectly processes Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) hosts containing unbalanced brackets, leading to a discrepancy in how the host is parsed by fast-uri compared to other HTTP clients. This host confusion can allow an attacker to bypass security policies, such as Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) denylists or redirect allowlists, by causing an application to evaluate its policy against an incorrect host string. This could result in unintended network requests or access to unauthorized resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: Host confusion via unbalanced URI brackets can bypass security policies
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit URI parsing discrepancies to bypass critical host-level access restrictions, such as SSRF filters or reverse proxy routing, without needing elevated privileges. Within Red Hat environments, the issue primarily impacts services that rely on fast-uri to validate external destinations before dispatching requests via Node.js HTTP clients. Product components that only provide frontend interfaces or do not evaluate host security policies using the parsed authority data are not exposed to security filter circumvention.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.

notes.text:
A flaw was found in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver for version < 1.17.10 and < 2.9.1. 
Improper handling of data query elements in the GridFS component can lead to a file identifier being misinterpreted as a query. An authenticated user can exploit this to delete all GridFS file chunks, making stored file content unreadable, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the MongoDB Go Driver. The GridFS component does not properly sanitize caller-supplied file identifiers before using them in database queries. A structured document passed as a file ID (for example, a BSON document containing query operators) is interpreted as a query condition rather than a literal match value. An authenticated attacker who can influence the file identifier passed to GridFS operations such as Delete, DownloadToStream, or OpenDownloadStream in an affected application can exploit this to delete all chunks in a GridFS bucket, resulting in permanent data loss and denial of service.
The practical impact depends on whether the product's code passes externally-controlled values as GridFS file identifiers.

- Validate file identifiers before passing them to GridFS operations. Ensure that file IDs supplied by users or external systems are scalar values (e.g., primitive.ObjectID or string) and reject any structured BSON documents or maps. This prevents query operator injection.
- Restrict who can supply GridFS file identifiers. Do not allow unauthenticated or low-privilege users to directly control the file ID parameter in GridFS API calls (Delete, OpenDownloadStream, DownloadToStream, etc.).

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve cached responses, including sensitive session credentials like Set-Cookie values, belonging to other users. This occurs because the component fails to properly validate security-zeroed cache entries when processing client `max-stale` directives. By requesting the same URL with a large `max-stale` value, an attacker can obtain another user's session credentials from shared-cache entries that were intended to be secure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: http-cache-semantics: http-cache-semantics: Information Disclosure via max-stale directive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can bypass shared-cache security controls over the network and expose sensitive session credentials belonging to other users. Red Hat products vendoring this library in client-only command-line tools or local development utilities are at reduced risk, as triggering the defect depends on an intermediary or shared cache mechanism processing client cache-control directives. Environments hosting multi-tenant web applications or reverse proxies that evaluate HTTP cache headers via this component face direct exposure to cross-session credential disclosure.
