notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. The lookupProperty own-property check returns Function.prototype.constructor before the prototype-method deny list is applied. When an attacker can render a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault enabled and an accessible function in the template context, arbitrary JavaScript can execute with the application process privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via Own Property Check Bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires rendering a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault set to true (off by default) and an accessible function in the template context, allowing bypass of the constructor deny list via Function.prototype. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because those non-default runtime conditions raise attack complexity (AC:H); default Handlebars configurations that keep allowProtoMethodsByDefault disabled are not exploitable for this issue.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. Incomplete validation of pre-parsed AST objects passed to compile() or precompile() allows unchecked AST fields to be emitted into generated JavaScript. An attacker who can supply an object instead of a template string can inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion in compile (Program.blockParams)
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires an application to pass a non-string object (for example, a JSON-deserialized value) to Handlebars.compile() or Handlebars.precompile(). Applications that only pass template strings are not affected. When that unsafe calling pattern is present, injected JavaScript can run with the privileges of the Node.js process. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because successful exploitation depends on that non-default API usage condition (AC:H), not on typical string-template pipelines alone.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost compress library. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a specially crafted Zstandard (zstd) compressed stream to an application using the library, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). Due to an integer handling error in the decompression logic, the decoder retains stale internal state and performs an out-of-bounds read, triggering an unhandled panic that crashes the application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via crafted zstd compressed input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost compress library's Zstandard (zstd) decompression implementation. An integer handling flaw in the FSE normalized count parsing logic allows a remote attacker to supply a specially crafted two-block compressed stream. When processed by vulnerable decode routines, the parser retains stale decode-table state and executes an out-of-bounds read, triggering an unhandled runtime panic. Applications decompressing untrusted inputs will terminate abruptly, causing a denial of service, while container boundaries and non-root execution isolate the impact from the underlying host.

remediations.details:
Reject or filter untrusted Zstandard-compressed payloads at ingress proxies, or restrict decompression endpoints to authenticated, trusted clients. No direct configuration-level workaround exists within the library itself.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-03) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce bounds on parsed count values and decode-table indices in klauspost/compress zstd decompression routines to prevent integer wraparound and out-of-bounds indexing: upgrade to klauspost/compress 1.20.2+ (or the corresponding fixed Red Hat builds), which reject counts exceeding math.MaxInt16 in readNCount, restrict Huffman-weight FSE tableLog values to 6 in huff0.ReadTable, and adjust count validation in validateNorm, closing crafted two-block zstd compressed stream. Until patched, this is a concern on applications decompressing untrusted Zstandard (zstd) input using klauspost/compress DecodeAll or streaming decoder, so reject or filter untrusted Zstandard-compressed payloads at ingress proxies, or restrict decompression endpoints to authenticated, trusted clients. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying integer wraparound defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1311 Input Size and Quantity Bounds Enforcement (high)

notes.text: A flaw was found in BuildKit. A malicious BuildKit client or frontend can craft a specially designed request, leading to the BuildKit daemon crashing. This vulnerability results in a denial of service (DoS), making the BuildKit service unavailable.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/moby/buildkit: BuildKit: Denial of Service via malicious client request
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: BuildKit is used by several Red Hat products to build container images. This issue allows a malicious BuildKit frontend or client to cause the BuildKit build process to crash. Exploiting this issue requires the ability to supply a build definition (for example, a Dockerfile specifying a custom #syntax frontend) to a BuildKit-based build; it does not allow remote code execution or exposure of data. The issue is fixed upstream in BuildKit version 0.31.2. Red Hat Hardened Images (Buildah, Podman, and Trivy) has already shipped the fixed version. Other affected Red Hat products are being assessed and will ship the fixed version of BuildKit in upcoming releases.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple key update messages in a single record after the handshake. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Go crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple TLS 1.3 key update messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: A flaw in the Go `crypto/tls` package allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service in applications using TLS 1.3. By sending multiple key update messages in a single record post-handshake, an attacker can trigger a connection deadlock, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption. This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `os.Root` functionality of Go on Unix systems. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass intended directory restrictions by crafting a path that ends with a symbolic link and a trailing slash. When a file is opened in `os.Root` with such a path, the symbolic link is improperly followed, potentially leading to access to locations outside of the defined root directory. This could result in information disclosure or unauthorized file system access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in Go's os.Root implementation. On Unix systems, `os.Root.Open()` improperly follows symlinks to locations outside the root directory when the path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., root.Open("symlink/")). This is because `openat()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` does not prevent symlink resolution when the path has a trailing /. An attacker able to create symlinks within an os.Root directory could use this to read or write files outside the intended root. The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected. This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

The following symbols are affected:
* `OpenInRoot`: Opens a file or directory within an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Create`: Creates a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Open`: Opens a path relative to an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenFile`: Opens a file with specified flags and permissions inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenRoot`: Opens a sub-root directory from an `os.Root`.
* `Root.ReadFile`: Reads a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.WriteFile`: Writes a file inside an `os.Root`.

There is no mitigation for this issue other than updating the Go toolchain to Go 1.25.12 or Go 1.26.5. Programs compiled with Go >= 1.24 that do not use the os.Root API are not affected by this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) package. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words. This could lead to excessive CPU consumption, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: mime: golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME header
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is rated as an Important severity flaw. A remote attacker could trigger a Denial of Service by sending a crafted MIME header with numerous invalid encoded-words to an application utilizing the affected Golang MIME package. This could lead to excessive CPU consumption on the system processing the malformed header, impacting service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in lxml, a library for processing XML and HTML in Python. The `lxml.html.defs.link_attrs` were missing `xlink:href`, which could allow an attacker to bypass URL filtering mechanisms. This vulnerability enables URL bypass attacks in embedded content such as Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) or Mathematical Markup Language (MathML), potentially leading to information disclosure or arbitrary code execution in the context of the user's browser.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: lxml: lxml-html-clean: lxml: URL bypass vulnerability in Cleaner via missing xlink:href
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker could inject malicious script schemes into rendered markup, resulting in cross-site scripting and potential session hijacking in the victim's browser. Exploitation requires an application to process untrusted user input using the HTML cleaner utility configured with non-default, relaxed attribute filtering. Under default library configurations where strict attribute allowlists are enforced, the relevant hyperlink attributes are stripped automatically before link scheme validation occurs.

notes.text: A flaw was found in WebOb, a library for HTTP requests and responses. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to bypass URL validation checks by injecting leading control characters or spaces into a redirect target. This can lead to an open redirect, enabling attackers to send users to malicious websites for phishing or to steal OAuth and Single Sign-On (SSO) tokens. Exploitation requires the user to follow the crafted redirect.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: webob: WebOb: Open redirect vulnerability leading to phishing and token theft
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an open redirect vulnerability in the WebOb library. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a malicious URL that, when processed by applications utilizing WebOb for redirects, bypasses URL validation. This could lead to users being redirected to attacker-controlled sites, facilitating phishing attacks or the theft of authentication tokens, provided the user follows the redirect.

remediations.details: Applications utilizing the WebOb library should implement strict validation of redirect target URLs. Configure applications to only allow redirects to trusted, fully-qualified URIs or to strictly allowlist permitted redirect destinations. Reject any redirect target that does not begin with an expected trusted host or a validated relative path, ensuring no leading whitespace or control characters are present.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/xml` package of Go. The `DecodeElement` function failed to correctly track recursion depth, which could lead to stack exhaustion. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML input, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.

notes.text: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important denial of service flaw affects applications utilizing the Go `encoding/xml` package. This vulnerability arises from an issue in XML decoding where a recursion depth counter fails to reset, potentially leading to stack exhaustion when processing malicious XML input.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Immutable.js, a library providing persistent immutable data structures. This vulnerability occurs when specific List operations, such as List#set or List#setSize, are provided with an index or size value within a particular large range. An attacker could exploit this by providing specially crafted input, leading to an uncatchable infinite loop or unbounded memory allocation, ultimately causing a Denial of Service (DoS) for applications using the library.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate impact denial of service vulnerability in Immutable.js affects Red Hat products that process untrusted input through List operations. An attacker can trigger an infinite loop or unbounded memory allocation by providing specially crafted large index values, leading to a service disruption. Additionally, silent data corruption may occur due to integer wrapping.

notes.text: A flaw was found in nanoid (Nano ID), a small, secure, and URL-friendly unique string ID generator. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a zero-size input to the customAlphabet or customRandom functions. This would cause an infinite loop, leading to a denial of service (DoS) condition by hanging the application's calling thread.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: nanoid: nanoid: Denial of Service via infinite loop in random ID generation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An algorithmic denial of service flaw was found in the `nanoid` library. When calling `customAlphabet` or `customRandom` with a `size` parameter of `0`, the internal generation loop fails to meet its termination condition. In Node.js or browser execution contexts, an attacker who supplies an unvalidated, zero-value size parameter to these functions causes the thread to enter an infinite loop, driving CPU utilization to 100% and completely blocking event loop execution for that thread.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go, a Go AMQP 0.9.1 client. A malicious or compromised AMQP broker can exploit this by advertising an extremely small frame size during connection negotiation. This can lead to excessive fragmentation of client publications, consuming significant CPU resources and potentially causing a Denial of Service (DoS) by stalling the client or its host.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Denial of Service via AMQP frame size negotiation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact for Red Hat environments because successful exploitation requires connecting to an untrusted or compromised AMQP broker, which is an uncommon prerequisite in standard managed cluster deployments. Red Hat services and operators utilizing this Go client typically communicate exclusively with trusted, internally administered message queues over secure channels. While an adversary controlling a broker endpoint could force excessive message packetization leading to resource exhaustion, confidentiality and integrity remain unimpacted.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go. The URI.String function in uri.go concatenates TLS asset path values directly into an AMQPS query string without proper encoding. If an application processes a TLS asset path containing special characters like ampersand or equals delimiters, these can be misinterpreted during URI re-parsing. This vulnerability could allow an attacker to overwrite connection options, potentially corrupting the connection configuration or selecting unintended local cryptographic assets, leading to a compromise of the TLS connection.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Connection configuration overwrite via unsanitized TLS path parameter injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact because applications in Red Hat products that use amqp091-go and accept attacker-controlled TLS asset paths can be induced to reparse a crafted AMQPS URI. A local attacker with partial control of a certificate, key, CA, or server-name path or related environment setting can inject query parameters and alter connection configuration, potentially selecting unintended local TLS material or causing connection failures.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go. The `Channel.Qos` function in `channel.go` incorrectly handles negative integer values for `prefetchCount` and `prefetchSize`, casting them to large unsigned integers. This allows an application that processes untrusted Quality of Service (QoS) configuration to request extremely high message prefetch limits. Consequently, a message broker can deliver a large volume of queued messages, leading to client memory exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Denial of Service via signed-to-unsigned integer casting
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact because applications using amqp091-go can be disrupted if untrusted QoS configuration supplies negative prefetch values. Those values can be converted to extremely large message limits, allowing excessive message delivery and memory exhaustion.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go, a Go AMQP 0.9.1 client. When the client synchronously sends events to application-provided channels, an unbuffered or full listener channel can cause the client's reader to block. This blockage prevents the processing of critical messages and heartbeats, leading to connection stalls, deadlocks, and disconnections. This vulnerability can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) for applications using the affected component.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Denial of Service due to synchronous event channel blocking
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact because a broker-driven event burst can block AMQP client processing when application notification channels are unbuffered, full, or not promptly drained. The resulting stall can cause missed heartbeats, deadlocks, or client disconnection.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go. A malicious or compromised broker can send an extreme declared message body size to a client. This causes the client to attempt an excessively large memory allocation without proper size capping, leading to memory exhaustion and termination of the client process. This vulnerability results in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Denial of Service via unbounded body buffer allocation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important severity for Red Hat products because an untrusted or rogue messaging broker can remotely force client services into an out-of-memory crash, resulting in a denial of service without requiring client-side privileges. In typical Red Hat deployments, AMQP clients connect exclusively to managed and authenticated messaging infrastructure within trusted internal networks, significantly reducing exposure to rogue brokers. While the issue results in immediate process termination for the consuming application, it does not permit arbitrary code execution or data leakage.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go. A malicious or compromised broker can send a specially crafted AMQP (Advanced Message Queuing Protocol) message with a malformed field length. This can cause an integer overflow, leading to a runtime panic in the client process. Consequently, the client process terminates, resulting in a denial of service.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact because a malicious or compromised AMQP broker can send a malformed field length that causes the client process to panic and terminate.

notes.text: A flaw was found in amqp091-go, a Go AMQP 0.9.1 client. A malicious AMQP broker could exploit this by sending oversized data frames, forcing the client to allocate excessive memory. This can lead to unexpected memory consumption and potentially cause the application to become unavailable, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: amqp091-go: Denial of Service via oversized AMQP payloads
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw in the amqp091-go client can lead to a denial of service in Red Hat products. A compromised or malicious AMQP broker could exploit this by sending oversized payloads, forcing the client to consume excessive memory and potentially causing application-layer service disruption. The impact is considered Important due to the potential for resource exhaustion and disruption of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in qs. The `qs.stringify` function, responsible for serializing objects, does not properly validate the `isBuffer` property of an object's constructor before attempting to invoke it. An unauthenticated attacker can provide specially crafted input that, when processed and then serialized by `qs.stringify`, triggers a `TypeError`. This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS), causing affected applications to return a 500 error or, in certain scenarios, terminate the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: qs: qs: Denial of Service via improper validation in stringify function
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A denial of service vulnerability was found in the qs package for Node.js. The stringify function does not verify that constructor.isBuffer is callable before invoking it. An attacker who can influence object shape, for example through query parameters parsed with allowPrototypes: true as Express 4 does by default, can cause qs.stringify to throw a TypeError when that data is re-serialized. In typical Node.js HTTP frameworks the error is caught per request and returns HTTP 500. In code paths without an error boundary, such as async handlers or background jobs, the process may exit.

notes.text: A flaw was found in js-yaml, a JavaScript YAML parser. An attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted YAML document that causes the parser to perform excessive processing when handling merge keys with empty sources. This can lead to prolonged CPU consumption, effectively causing a denial of service (DoS) for applications that process untrusted YAML input.

notes.text: js-yaml: js-yaml: Denial of Service vulnerability in YAML parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in js-yaml, affecting applications that process untrusted YAML input. The flaw allows an attacker to craft a small YAML document that, when parsed, can lead to prolonged CPU consumption due to inefficient merge key processing, potentially exhausting system resources. This is particularly relevant where applications handle external YAML data and have merge processing enabled by default.

notes.text: A flaw was found in source-map-js. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to trigger a denial of service by providing malformed input. Specifically, by supplying extremely large offset line values in indexed source maps, the attacker can cause the service's event loop to block, making it unable to process further requests.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: source-map-js: source-map-js: Denial of Service via malformed indexed source maps
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can supply crafted data that synchronously blocks the single-threaded event loop, resulting in a sustained denial of service for affected services. In standard Red Hat application environments, source map parsing utilities are predominantly utilized in build systems or developer tooling rather than production-facing services, which limits general exposure. However, server-side applications accepting and processing untrusted source maps from external clients are directly susceptible to availability disruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Podman. When a container image with checkpoint annotations is executed using the podman run command, Podman treats the image as a restored checkpoint and ignores user-specified sandboxing options, such as dropped privileges. An attacker can exploit this issue by enticing a user to run a specially crafted image, leading to a container sandbox bypass and potential execution with elevated system privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: podman: podman: The `podman run` command can be instructed to disable almost all sandboxing - including user-requested sandboxing - by image annotation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important severity impact for Red Hat environments because running a malicious image can completely circumvent expected confinement boundaries and grant unexpected privileges to a container, compromising host integrity. Under default configurations, container execution relies on enforced sandboxing limits and security flags supplied by the operator. However, if an image embeds specific checkpoint metadata, the runtime automatically prioritizes the checkpoint configuration over explicit command-line restrictions, silently omitting requested security controls. Exploitation requires an operator or automated workflow to launch an untrusted image; environments that execute only vetted container workloads from trusted registries remain at reduced operational risk.

notes.text: A flaw was found in urllib3. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker on the network to intercept and alter data transmitted through an HTTPS proxy. The issue occurs when target-server Transport Layer Security (TLS) settings inadvertently overwrite the proxy's TLS configuration, which can disable certificate verification on reused connection contexts. Consequently, an attacker can impersonate the proxy to monitor or modify forwarded traffic or capture client credentials.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: urllib3: urllib3: Traffic interception via HTTPS proxy TLS configuration override
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important impact because a network attacker can exploit corrupted TLS validation states to impersonate an HTTPS proxy, enabling complete interception and manipulation of sensitive communications as well as client credential theft. Successful exploitation depends on specialized application architectures where outgoing requests utilize an HTTPS-capable proxy alongside customized destination TLS parameters that inadvertently override proxy verification. Default Red Hat enterprise deployments that communicate directly with endpoints, utilize traditional HTTP proxies, or rely on standard CONNECT tunneling for end-to-end encryption do not expose this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in urllib3. This flaw allows a Denial of Service (DoS) through unbounded memory allocation when parsing chunk-encoded responses. A malicious server can send an excessively long chunk-size line without a newline, exhausting client memory and terminating the application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: urllib3: urllib3: Denial of Service via unbounded memory allocation in chunk parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because an untrusted remote server can trigger process crashes and complete denial of service across client applications without requiring authentication or special privileges. In Red Hat environments, urllib3 is integrated across numerous system tools, container workloads, and platform services to handle outbound web communication. The risk specifically manifests when these services process streamed replies from potentially malicious third-party endpoints, whereas workloads restricted to internal or verified infrastructure remain largely unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. When retrieving cryptographic keys from a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint, PyJWKClient fails to validate HTTP redirect destinations against trusted domain boundaries. A remote attacker who can influence the response of a trusted endpoint can redirect key requests to an untrusted server, allowing the client to accept forged verification keys or potentially exposing sensitive credentials.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Verification key substitution via unvalidated JWKS redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because improper handling of HTTP redirects during dynamic key retrieval can allow an adversary to supply forged cryptographic keys or intercept sensitive request headers. In Red Hat environments where services utilize PyJWKClient to fetch JSON Web Key Sets over the network, accepting untrusted key material may compromise token validation and authentication boundaries. Exploitation requires the target service to dynamically resolve keys via HTTP and relies on an attacker's ability to manipulate responses returned by the configured key server.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. When an application allows both symmetric and asymmetric signing algorithms, minor formatting variations in a public key can prevent the library from properly identifying it as an asymmetric key. Consequently, the library improperly treats the public key as a shared secret key, allowing a remote attacker to forge valid authentication tokens and bypass security controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: PyJWT: Authentication bypass via improper public key validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Critical severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker could forge valid cryptographic tokens and bypass authentication checks without knowing the private signing key. Exploitation occurs when consuming applications configure token verification to accept both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms simultaneously, allowing an asymmetric public key to be mishandled as a symmetric secret. Deployments that strictly enforce a single algorithm type or validate tokens using JSON Web Key sets do not permit this algorithm confusion and remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyjwt. When verifying cryptographic keys, the raw JSON Web Key (JWK) parser fails to normalize Unicode byte-order marks (BOM). In mixed-algorithm verification environments, an attacker who knows the public key can supply a key prefixed with a byte-order mark, causing the system to misidentify the public key as a shared symmetric secret. This flaw allows an attacker to forge authenticated JSON Web Tokens (JWT) and bypass authentication controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Token forgery via improper Unicode byte-order mark handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity because successful exploitation permits an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and forge valid tokens, though exploitation requires specific mixed-algorithm verification settings. In Red Hat environments, exposure is restricted to services that simultaneously allow both symmetric HMAC and asymmetric signature algorithms while parsing public keys that contain byte order marks. Workloads and services that enforce single-algorithm verification policies or utilize standard asymmetric key validation routines are not susceptible to this attack.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication by forging arbitrary JSON Web Tokens (JWTs). When an application allows both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms, PyJWT fails to properly validate public JSON Web Key (JWK) container representations, mistakenly accepting public key material as a symmetric Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) secret. As a result, an attacker with knowledge of the public key can generate validly signed tokens with arbitrary authenticated claims.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Token forgery via acceptance of public JWK containers as HMAC secrets
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as Important because an attacker with access to a public verification key can forge cryptographic tokens to bypass authentication, allowing impersonation of privileged users and unauthorized access to protected application resources. Exploitation is limited to environments where applications concurrently permit symmetric HMAC and asymmetric algorithms while passing public key containers into validation routines.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pypdf. By supplying a specially crafted PDF document containing excessively long indirect object identifiers or generation tokens without whitespace, a remote attacker can trigger unbounded input scanning during parsing. This issue causes significant processing delays and excessive resource consumption, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) and application unavailability.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pypdf: pypdf: Denial of Service via crafted indirect object tokens in PDF files
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important impact flaw can make a Red Hat service unavailable when pypdf parses a crafted PDF with excessively long indirect-object tokens.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pypdf. This vulnerability allows an attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by providing a specially crafted PDF document with an oversized font character width array. When processing the document during operations such as text extraction, the library allocates excessive memory, leading to resource exhaustion and potential application failure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pypdf: pypdf: Denial of Service via excessive memory consumption during font parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important impact flaw can exhaust memory when a Red Hat service extracts text from a crafted PDF with an oversized font width array.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pypdf. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing a crafted PDF document containing a partially malformed FlateDecode data compression stream. When processing the malformed stream, the application triggers an inefficient recovery routine that consumes excessive processing time, potentially resulting in application unresponsiveness and a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: pypdf: pypdf: Denial of Service via crafted FlateDecode stream
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important impact flaw can consume excessive processing time when a Red Hat service decodes a malformed FlateDecode stream in a crafted PDF.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pypdf. A remote attacker can exploit this issue by submitting a specially crafted PDF document with specific form field values. When an application updates these fields with flattening enabled, redundant computational operations are repeated inside a loop during appearance stream generation. This excessive workload consumes processing resources, leading to application unresponsiveness and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pypdf: pypdf: Denial of Service via crafted PDF form fields
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important impact flaw can exhaust resources when a Red Hat product uses pypdf to flatten form fields in a crafted PDF; ordinary PDF reading does not trigger it.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pypdf. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted PDF document containing a large number of embedded files. When an application accesses the attachment mapping, the library repeatedly reparses the entire attachment list for each lookup. This repetitive processing consumes excessive computational resources, leading to severe performance degradation and unresponsiveness.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important impact flaw can consume excessive processing time when a Red Hat product accesses pypdf’s attachment mapping for a crafted PDF with many embedded files.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pypdf. By supplying a specially crafted PDF file containing unusually large alphabetical page-label values, a remote attacker can trigger excessive memory allocation when an application retrieves document page labels. This uncontrolled memory consumption can cause the application to crash or become unresponsive, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important impact flaw can exhaust memory when a Red Hat product retrieves page labels from a crafted PDF containing unusually large alphabetical label values.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Quay where the robot account listing function constructs a SQL LIKE pattern from user-controlled namespace names without escaping wildcard metacharacters. An attacker who creates a namespace containing an underscore character can match and retrieve robot accounts and their decrypted authentication tokens from other tenants' namespaces, leading to cross-tenant credential theft and unauthorized image operations.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: quay: quay: SQL LIKE wildcard injection in robot listing leaks cross-tenant robot tokens
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is rated Critical because it lets an authenticated attacker break tenant isolation in multi-tenant Quay deployments. By creating a namespace whose name contains an underscore that collides with an existing one, the attacker causes the underscore to act as a single-character SQL LIKE wildcard, matching the victim's namespace. This allows the attacker to list and steal the victim's robot account tokens, then use them to read, push, or overwrite that tenant's container images. No elevated privileges or victim interaction are required. In OpenShift environments where Quay serves as the integrated container registry, stolen robot credentials can be used to inject malicious images into CI/CD pipelines, putting the container supply chain across production clusters at risk. Multi-tenant Quay deployments are common in enterprises sharing a registry across teams and in service providers hosting multiple customer organizations.

Update to the fixed Red Hat Quay release for your version: 3.9.28, 3.10.28, 3.12.24, 3.14.10, 3.15.9, 3.16.7, 3.17.7, or 3.18.3. Red Hat has already fixed Quay.io. There is no other complete workaround.
If you cannot update immediately, restrict who can create organizations or namespaces containing an underscore, rotate robot tokens for any namespace that collides with an underscore-containing one, and monitor registry activity for pulls or pushes that don't match expected robot usage. These steps reduce exposure but do not fix the underlying flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted Microsoft Image Composer (MIC) file. When an application attempts to count or extract frames from the malicious image, an improper state reset triggers an infinite loop. This non-advancing loop consumes excessive CPU resources and can hang application worker processes indefinitely.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via infinite loop during crafted MIC image parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can induce an infinite loop, exhausting worker CPU resources and resulting in a denial of service for applications handling untrusted image data. Within Red Hat environments, Pillow is deployed across numerous container images, machine learning frameworks, and automated backend services. Exploitation requires the optional olefile dependency to be present to register the Microsoft Image Composer format handler, and specifically targets workflows that query frame counts or process multi-frame images. Environments that do not inspect frame counts or do not have olefile installed are not vulnerable.

Image Composer (MIC) file with an embedded TIFF containing three or more IFDs. As a compensating measure, Impose CPU time limits using ulimit or prlimit to terminate worker processes caught in the non-advancing MIC image parsing loop before system CPU is exhausted and Configure service watchdogs with automatic restart under systemd to detect stalled processes via keep-alives and restore availability. notes.text: A flaw was found in oauthlib. In certain token grant flows, the authorization system can authenticate an incoming client while retaining a different, client-supplied identifier for permission and scope validation. A remote, authenticated attacker with lower privileges can exploit this inconsistency by submitting another client's identifier during token requests. This flaw leads to privilege escalation, potentially allowing the attacker to obtain access tokens with unauthorized permissions and scopes associated with another client.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: oauthlib: oauthlib: privilege escalation via client identity confusion in token grant handlers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity for Red Hat products because an authenticated client with low privileges can obtain access tokens under a different identity over the network, leading to significant privilege escalation without requiring user interaction. The exposure specifically impacts deployments where the server application relies on the submitted client identifier parameter during scope or grant checks instead of the authenticated client object. Workloads that do not act as an OAuth2 token endpoint or that enforce scope authorization solely from the authenticated entity remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Red Hat Quay. An unauthenticated client can obtain an anonymous registry token with an audience it controls, present that token to the service key rotation endpoint, and install its own approved signing key with no expiry. Registry tokens signed with that key are accepted for any repository, allowing read and write access to private images and replacement of repository tags.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: quay: Red Hat Quay: unauthenticated registry signing-key takeover via service key rotation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Critical flaw in Red Hat Quay's service key server allows an unauthenticated attacker to take over registry token signing. Key rotation authenticates the caller only by verifying that the JWT is signed by an already approved service key with the expected audience and issuer, without checking that the token is a rotation credential. An anonymous token minted by /v2/auth satisfies that check. Installed keys inherit approval and can be created without an expiry, so forged registry tokens are accepted for any repository. Deployments where /keys is reachable by untrusted clients are affected.

notes.text:
rhc is a client tool and daemon that connects the system to Red Hat hosted services enabling system and subscription management.

Security Fix(es):

* crypto/tls: crypto/tls: Incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption (CVE-2025-68121)

* golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root (CVE-2026-32282)

* crypto/tls: golang: Go crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple TLS 1.3 key update messages (CVE-2026-32283)

* crypto/x509: crypto/tls: golang: Go: Denial of Service vulnerability in certificate chain building (CVE-2026-32280)

* golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing (CVE-2026-39821)

* mime: golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME header (CVE-2026-42504)

* crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries (CVE-2026-27145)

* encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal (CVE-2026-33818)

* net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution (CVE-2026-56860)

* html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input (CVE-2026-56858)

* crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages (CVE-2026-56862)

* net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers (CVE-2026-78667)

* crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references (CVE-2026-97031)

* net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing (CVE-2026-94440)

* net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames (CVE-2026-78669)

* crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates (CVE-2026-111943)

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in the crypto/tls component. This vulnerability occurs during Transport Layer Security (TLS) session resumption when certificate authority (CA) settings are modified between the initial and resumed handshakes. An attacker could exploit this to bypass certificate validation, allowing a client or server to establish a connection that should have been rejected. This could lead to an authentication bypass under specific conditions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: crypto/tls: Incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.

notes.text: golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

notes.text:
yggdrasil is a system daemon that subscribes to topics on an MQTT broker and routes any data received on the topics to an appropriate child "worker" process, exchanging data with its worker processes through a D-Bus message broker.

* crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages (CVE-2026-56862)

* net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames (CVE-2026-78669)

cwe.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.
notes.title: Statement

vulnerabilities.title: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Excessive Platform Resource Consumption within a Loop

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.
notes.title: Statement

vulnerabilities.title: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in crypto/tls. A remote attacker can trigger this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet containing multiple Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) outer extension references to a server. Processing these unauthorized references leads to excessive memory consumption, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) through server crashes or unresponsiveness.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory exhaustion and crash server processes without requiring privileges or user interaction. Go applications that terminate TLS connections and accept Encrypted Client Hello configurations are vulnerable to resource amplification during the initial handshake. While the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data confidentiality, the resulting denial of service can disrupt critical network services.

notes.text:
An update for grafana-pcp is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
The Grafana plugin for Performance Co-Pilot includes datasources for scalable time series from pmseries and Redis, live PCP metrics and bpftrace scripts from pmdabpftrace, as well as several dashboards.

Security Fix(es):

* encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal (CVE-2026-33818)

* net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution (CVE-2026-56860)

* net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service (CVE-2026-56853)

* html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input (CVE-2026-56858)

* crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages (CVE-2026-56862)

* crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references (CVE-2026-97031)

* net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing (CVE-2026-94440)

* net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames (CVE-2026-78669)

* crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates (CVE-2026-111943)

Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s):

* vLLM AI dashboard issues [10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-271171)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the mime/multipart and net/textproto packages in Go. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted multipart form request that bypasses configured memory limits when the remaining boundary limit is small. This issue allows the application to read an arbitrarily long line into memory, leading to excessive resource consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate severity for Red Hat products because, while an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger excessive memory consumption leading to a denial of service, exploitation cannot lead to code execution or information disclosure. The issue specifically threatens Go-based services and daemons that accept and process incoming multipart HTTP form payloads. Applications built with Go that do not expose web interfaces or parse multipart request streams are unaffected by this flaw.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in crypto/tls. A remote attacker can trigger this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet containing multiple Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) outer extension references to a server. Processing these unauthorized references leads to excessive memory consumption, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) through server crashes or unresponsiveness.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory exhaustion and crash server processes without requiring privileges or user interaction. Go applications that terminate TLS connections and accept Encrypted Client Hello configurations are vulnerable to resource amplification during the initial handshake. While the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data confidentiality, the resulting denial of service can disrupt critical network services.
notes.title: Statement
